definitions.explanation: Left to one's own choice or discretion; not compulsory. Commonly seen on forms, in instructions, and in legal contexts.
Chosen without specific criteria; any value or element that satisfies certain conditions. Used in technical and academic contexts.

examples.japanese: この{項目|こうもく}は{任意|にんい}です。
{任意|にんい}の{保険|ほけん}に{加入|かにゅう}するかどうかは{本人|ほんにん}が{決|き}めることだ。
examples.english: Whether to enroll in optional insurance is for the individual to decide.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}が{任意|にんい}で{事情聴取|じじょうちょうしゅ}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: The police conducted a voluntary interview.

examples.japanese: {任意|にんい}の{正|せい}の{整数|せいすう}nについて{成|な}り{立|た}つ。
examples.english: This holds for any positive integer n.

examples.japanese: {任意|にんい}の{点|てん}Pを{選|えら}び、そこから{直線|ちょくせん}を{引|ひ}く。
examples.english: Choose an arbitrary point P and draw a line from it.

examples.japanese: この{定理|ていり}は{任意|にんい}の{三角形|さんかくけい}に{適用|てきよう}できる。
examples.english: This theorem can be applied to any triangle.

notes:
USAGE:
{任意|にんい} is used as a no-adjective ({任意|にんい}の) or as a noun. In everyday Japanese, it most often means "optional" or "voluntary." In police and legal contexts, {任意|にんい} contrasts with {強制|きょうせい} (compulsory).
In police terminology, {任意|にんい} (voluntary questioning/accompaniment) contrasts with {逮捕|たいほ} (arrest). While technically voluntary, {任意|にんい}{同行|どうこう} in practice is difficult to refuse.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {任意|にんい}{加入|かにゅう} (voluntary enrollment)
- {任意|にんい}{保険|ほけん} (optional insurance)
- {任意|にんい}{同行|どうこう} (voluntary accompaniment to police station)
- {任意|にんい}の{値|あたい} (any value)
